message.content:
Below are two ways to spin up a **Google Cloud Compute Engine** instance that has an **NVIDIA RTX A6000** GPU and boots from **Ubuntu 20.04 LTS**.

> **NOTE**  
> *Google Cloud does not use the “EC2” terminology – that’s AWS. In GCP the service is called **Compute Engine**.*  
> *The RTX A6000 is available as the GPU type `nvidia-tesla-a6000`.*

---

## 1.  `gcloud` CLI (recommended)

```bash
# 1️⃣  Set your project and zone
PROJECT_ID="my-gcp-project"
ZONE="us-central1-a"

# 2️⃣  Create the instance
gcloud compute instances create rtx-a6000-ubuntu \
  --project=${PROJECT_ID} \
  --zone=${ZONE} \
  --machine-type=n1-standard-8 \          # 8 vCPU, 30 GB RAM (adjust as needed)
  --accelerator=type=nvidia-tesla-a6000,count=1 \
  --image-family=ubuntu-2004-lts \
  --image-project=ubuntu-os-cloud \
  --boot-disk-size=100GB \
  --boot-disk-type=pd-ssd \
  --maintenance-policy=MIGRATE \
  --restart-on-failure \
  --metadata-from-file startup-script=startup.sh \   # optional init script
  --tags=http-server,https-server \
  --scopes=https://www.googleapis.com/auth/cloud-platform
```

### What each flag does

| Flag | Purpose |
|------|---------|
| `--machine-type` | CPU/RAM configuration. `n1-standard-8` gives 8 vCPUs & 30 GB RAM. |
| `--accelerator` | Adds the GPU. `count=1` gives a single RTX A6000. |
| `--image-family` & `--image-project` | Boots from the latest Ubuntu 20.04 LTS image. |
| `--boot-disk-size` & `--boot-disk-type` | SSD boot disk of 100 GB. |
| `--maintenance-policy=MIGRATE` | VM will be live‑migrated during maintenance. |
| `--restart-on-failure` | Auto‑restart if the VM crashes. |
| `--metadata-from-file startup-script` | Optional shell script that runs on first boot. |
| `--tags` | Enables HTTP/HTTPS firewall rules if you need them. |
| `--scopes` | Grants the VM full Cloud Platform access (adjust scopes if you want tighter security). |

> **Tip:** If you need more RAM or CPUs, pick a different machine type (e.g., `n1-highmem-8`, `n1-highcpu-8`, or a custom type).

---

## 2.  REST API (curl)

If you prefer to use the raw REST API, here’s a `curl` example that posts a JSON payload to the Compute Engine endpoint.

```bash
# 1️⃣  Set variables
PROJECT_ID="my-gcp-project"
ZONE="us-central1-a"
INSTANCE_NAME="rtx-a6000-ubuntu"
ACCESS_TOKEN=$(gcloud auth application-default print-access-token)

# 2️⃣  Build the JSON body
read -r -d '' INSTANCE_JSON <<EOF
{
  "name": "$INSTANCE_NAME",
  "machineType": "zones/$ZONE/machineTypes/n1-standard-8",
  "disks": [
    {
      "boot": true,
      "autoDelete": true,
      "initializeParams": {
        "sourceImage": "projects/ubuntu-os-cloud/global/images/family/ubuntu-2004-lts",
        "diskSizeGb": 100,
        "diskType": "projects/$PROJECT_ID/zones/$ZONE/diskTypes/pd-ssd"
      }
    }
  ],
  "networkInterfaces": [
    {
      "network": "global/networks/default",
      "accessConfigs": [
        { "type": "ONE_TO_ONE_NAT", "name": "External NAT" }
      ]
    }
  ],
  "guestAccelerators": [
    {
      "acceleratorType": "projects/$PROJECT_ID/zones/$ZONE/acceleratorTypes/nvidia-tesla-a6000",
      "acceleratorCount": 1
    }
  ],
  "scheduling": {
    "preemptible": false,
    "onHostMaintenance": "MIGRATE",
    "automaticRestart": true
  },
  "metadata": {
    "items": [
      {
        "key": "startup-script",
        "value": "#!/bin/bash\napt-get update\napt-get install -y nvidia-driver-535"
      }
    ]
  }
}
EOF

# 3️⃣  POST the request
curl -X POST \
  "https://compute.googleapis.com/compute/v1/projects/${PROJECT_ID}/zones/${ZONE}/instances" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d "${INSTANCE_JSON}"
```

### Explanation of the JSON payload

| Field | Meaning |
|-------|---------|
| `name` | Instance name. |
| `machineType` | Full URL to the machine type. |
| `disks[0]` | Boot disk configuration (Ubuntu 20.04 LTS, 100 GB SSD). |
| `networkInterfaces[0]` | Default VPC network with external NAT. |
| `guestAccelerators[0]` | Adds one RTX A6000 GPU. |
| `scheduling` | Live‑migration enabled, auto‑restart on failure. |
| `metadata.items[0]` | Optional startup script (installs NVIDIA driver). |

> **Prerequisites**  
> *Enable the Compute Engine API.*  
> *Make sure the service account you’re using has the `roles/compute.instanceAdmin.v1` role.*  
> *The `access_token` can be obtained via `gcloud auth application-default print-access-token` or by using OAuth 2.0 flow.*

---

## Quick Checklist

| ✅ | Item |
|----|------|
| 1 | Project ID & zone set |
| 2 | Compute Engine API enabled |
| 3 | Proper IAM permissions (`compute.instanceAdmin.v1`) |
| 4 | GPU quota for `nvidia-tesla-a6000` in your region |
| 5 | (Optional) Firewall rules for SSH/HTTP/HTTPS |
| 6 | (Optional) Startup script to install NVIDIA drivers |

Once the instance is running, you can SSH into it:

```bash
gcloud compute ssh rtx-a6000-ubuntu --project=${PROJECT_ID} --zone=${ZONE}
```

And verify the GPU:

```bash
nvidia-smi
```

That’s it! You now have a Compute Engine VM with an RTX A6000 GPU running Ubuntu 20.04 LTS.
